channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Medical Fund Explains Delays in Payments to Healthcare Organizations
item.description: The Fund for Social Health Insurance (FSHI) in Kazakhstan attributes payment delays to healthcare organizations to ongoing adjustments in regulatory requirements by the Ministry of Health. These changes affected tariffs, funding sources, and financing procedures, with IT systems struggling to keep pace. Corrections are ongoing for services rendered from July to October.

item.title: Kazakhstan Court Upholds Consumer Rights Against Airline FlyArystan
item.description: A Kazakh court has upheld a Ministry of Trade and Integration order against airline FlyArystan. The ruling confirms the illegality of several airline rules that infringed upon passenger rights, including unilateral changes to carriage conditions and restrictions on refunds. The airline's appeal was rejected.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Initiative for International Water Organization to be Discussed at UN Conference
item.description: Kazakhstan's proposal to establish an International Water Organization will be discussed at the upcoming UN Water Resources Conference in Abu Dhabi. Representatives from Senegal and the UAE have supported the initiative, emphasizing the importance of joint action to address water scarcity. The briefing in New York highlighted the need for international cooperation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Four Sectors Could Attract Over $500 Million in Investments, World Bank Study Finds
item.description: A World Bank and IFC study indicates that Kyrgyzstan's fruit and berry processing, tourism, garment manufacturing, and trout farming sectors could attract over $500 million in private investment and create up to 67,600 jobs. Reforms are needed to simplify land access, improve certification, and develop infrastructure.

item.title: Emirates Airline Considers Launching Flights to Uzbekistan, Uzbekistan Airports Reports
item.description: Emirates Group representatives met with Uzbekistan Airports to discuss potential regular flights to Uzbekistan. The airline is evaluating factors like passenger traffic, market demand, and airport capabilities before making a decision. This move could boost tourism and international air connectivity for Uzbekistan.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Sovereign Credit Rating Raised to BB+ by S&P Global Ratings
item.description: S&P Global Ratings has upgraded Uzbekistan's sovereign credit rating to BB+ with a stable outlook, marking the country's highest rating ever. This upgrade reflects ongoing economic reforms, balanced financial policies, and strategic direction, bringing Uzbekistan one step closer to the investment grade BBB-.

item.title: Faizabad Residents Complain of Frequent Power Outages Disrupting Daily Life
item.description: Residents of Faizabad, the capital of Badakhshan province, are experiencing persistent power disruptions and frequent outages. They report that continuous blackouts disrupt daily lives, causing problems for families and shopkeepers. Residents are urging Taliban officials to address the irregular electricity supply.

item.title: Astana Increases Hospital Beds Amid Rise in ARVI and Flu Cases
item.description: Astana has increased hospital bed capacity and enhanced services at polyclinics and emergency services due to a seasonal rise in ARVI and flu cases. Currently, 313 patients, including 220 children and 30 pregnant women, are hospitalized with these illnesses.

item.title: US Department of Agriculture Payment System Hit by Cyberattack
item.description: Hackers breached the U.S. Department of Agriculture's payment system used to distribute funds to farmers. The department was notified of the incident, but it remains unclear who was responsible for the cyber intrusion.

item.title: FlyArystan Loses Court Case Over Passenger Ticket Refund Restrictions
item.description: Kazakhstan's FlyArystan airline lost a court case challenging regulations that restricted passenger ticket refunds and additional payments. The Ministry of Trade and Integration found the airline violated consumer rights, a decision upheld by the court.

item.title: Uzbekistan Police Arrest Suspects in Nearly $100 Million Bank Card Theft Scheme
item.description: Police in Nukus, Uzbekistan, have arrested a group suspected of stealing nearly 1 billion soms from citizens' bank cards. The suspects allegedly distributed malicious APK files via Telegram to gain access to financial information. Stolen funds were used to purchase electronics, pay online microloans, and fund betting accounts. Authorities urge the public to avoid installing unknown APKs and sharing banking details.

item.title: FlyArystan Loses Court Battle Over Internal Rules Restricting Passenger Rights
item.description: The airline FlyArystan has lost a court case concerning its internal rules that restricted passenger rights. A court upheld a directive from the Ministry of Trade and Integration for the airline to rectify violations. An investigation found FlyArystan's rules illegally charged for services, hindered refunds, and violated information disclosure procedures. The airline's appeal was also rejected.

item.title: Gishtkoprik Border Customs Post to Open on November 25, Expected to Serve 70,000 Daily
item.description: The "Gishtkoprik" border customs post, which was scheduled to open in September, is now set to commence operations on November 25. The renovated post is designed to handle approximately 70,000 passengers and over 2,000 vehicles daily, according to a source from the Kazakh Embassy.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Holds Training on Drinking Water and Wastewater Tariffs
item.description: Around 100 representatives from all regions of Kyrgyzstan participated in a two-day training on calculating tariffs for drinking water and wastewater. The event, organized by the Department for the Development of Drinking Water Supply and Wastewater, focused on tariff formation, loss reduction, and service accessibility. International experts shared experiences in tariff regulation from other countries.

item.title: Swiss Aid Agency: Relations with Taliban Limited to Technical and Humanitarian Matters
item.description: The Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC) in Afghanistan states its engagement with the Taliban is restricted to technical and humanitarian coordination. SDC Head Eric Marclay confirmed no funds are paid to the Taliban, with priorities focused on vulnerable populations. Projects are officially approved by Taliban authorities but do not imply active cooperation.

item.title: Tajikistan to Establish Trade House in Minsk to Boost Economic Ties
item.description: Tajikistan and Belarus discussed strengthening trade and economic relations, including the creation of a Tajik Trade House in Minsk. This initiative aims to promote Tajik goods, increase exports, and facilitate market access for local producers in Belarus.

item.title: Kazakhstan Seeks Alternative Routes for Coal Exports Amid Transit Issues
item.description: Kazakhstan is exploring alternative routes for its coal exports due to Russian Railways' refusal to approve transit to Baltic Sea ports. Kazakhstan Temir Zholy is working with neighboring countries to maintain stable export transportation and protect the interests of domestic shippers.

item.title: UN Warns Restrictions Deny Afghan Women Vital Healthcare Access
item.description: UN Women reports that restrictions imposed on women and girls in Afghanistan, combined with funding cuts, are severely limiting their access to essential healthcare. Over 100 edicts have restricted movement and employment, impacting millions. Nearly 300 health facilities have closed, affecting over a million women and girls.

item.title: Kazakhstan Deports 77 Foreigners for Migration Law Violations
item.description: During the 'Illegal Migrant - 2026' operation, Kazakhstan deported 77 foreign citizens by court order for violating migration laws. Police identified 293 cases of migration law breaches. Fifteen employers were held accountable for hiring foreign nationals without proper permits. Three Kazakh citizens and one foreigner were detained for aiding illegal border crossings.

item.title: Switzerland Reopens Kabul Office to Aid Afghans, Limits Taliban Contact
item.description: Switzerland has reopened its humanitarian office in Kabul to address the basic needs of the Afghan people without legitimizing the Taliban. Swiss officials stated that contact with the Taliban remains limited to technical coordination on environmental protection, returnee assistance, and mine clearance. The country is a significant humanitarian supporter of Afghanistan.

item.title: US Lawmakers Urge Halt to Funding for Offensive Operations Against Iran
item.description: Two Democratic US Congress members, Yassamin Ansari and Ro Khanna, are calling for an end to funding offensive military operations against Iran. They argue that funds should be redirected to domestic priorities, citing US midterm election results and rising costs of living. They urge Congress to act before the December 11 deadline.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Secures $95.75 Million Loan for Irrigation System Modernization
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has signed a $95.75 million loan agreement with the International Development Association (IDA), part of the World Bank Group, to modernize its irrigation systems. The funds will support the national investment program, aiming to improve water supply to 82,000 hectares of agricultural land and benefit over 454,000 residents by 2032.

item.title: Kazakhstan Presents Experience in Returning Citizens from Syria and Iraq to OSCE
item.description: Kazakhstan shared its experience in the repatriation and social adaptation of citizens from Syria and Iraq at an OSCE briefing in Astana. The operations "Zhusan" and "Rusafa" successfully returned 756 individuals, including 528 children. Kazakhstan proposed establishing a regional working group to coordinate efforts for protecting affected citizens.

item.title: S&P Raises Uzbekistan's Credit Rating to BB+, Highest in Country's History
item.description: S&P Global Ratings has upgraded Uzbekistan's credit rating to BB+, the highest level in the country's history. This upgrade brings Uzbekistan one step closer to achieving an investment-grade rating. The new rating reflects the country's improving economic stability and outlook.

item.title: Kazakhstan Confiscates Nearly 3,000 Hectares from Company Abandoning Investment Project
item.description: In the East Kazakhstan region, nearly 3,000 hectares of land, valued at 180 million tenge, have been returned to state ownership. A company abandoned its investment project and failed to return the unused land. The prosecutor's office intervened to reclaim the 2,930 hectares.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan Address Border Congestion Issues at Key Crossing
item.description: Trucks have been experiencing significant delays at the 'Baurzhan Konysbayev' border crossing between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan. Kazakhstan's State Revenue Committee attributes congestion to a 16.2% increase in vehicle flow and the electronic queue system. Plans are underway to redirect traffic to the 'Atameken-Gulistan' checkpoint.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's "Kyrgyzaltyn" Reports Over $900 Million Profit in Nine Months
item.description: JSC "Kyrgyzaltyn" announced a revenue exceeding 131 billion soms and a net profit of over 82.3 billion soms for the first nine months of 2026. Over the past five years, the company's net profit surpassed 90 billion soms. Strategic mineral resources are now directed towards state interests.

item.title: Iran's IRGC Claims to Have Shot Down US MQ-9 Drone Over Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claims to have intercepted and shot down a US MQ-9 drone over the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC stated it was the 58th US military drone downed by Iran. The US military has not confirmed or denied the claim, having previously dismissed similar assertions as false.

item.title: Four Arrested in Kazakhstan for Organizing Illegal Migration
item.description: Four individuals, including three Kazakh citizens and one foreigner, have been detained in the Zhambyl region on suspicion of organizing illegal border crossings. Police have launched a criminal case and placed all suspects in temporary detention. The operation also uncovered 293 migration law violations.

item.title: Trump Aims for Ukraine Peace Deal by January 2027, Report Says
item.description: US President Donald Trump's administration has informed Ukraine and the EU of Washington's desire for a peace agreement with Russia by early January 2027, according to the Financial Times. The White House reportedly aims to finalize a deal before potential Democratic control of Congress.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Malaysia Discuss Railway Cooperation and New Transport Links
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Malaysia have agreed to exchange expert visits to explore railway sector cooperation. They are considering freight transport development between Central and Southeast Asia, linked to the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway project. This could expand ASEAN markets' access to Central Asia, the Middle East, and Europe.

item.title: Illegal Call Center in Tashkent Uncovered, Involved in Crypto Asset Fraud
item.description: An illegal online call center operated by 10 individuals in Tashkent has been shut down. The group allegedly defrauded European citizens by offering fake documents and trading/crypto education, then transferring victims' crypto assets. Approximately $2.4 million in crypto assets were involved.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans to Attract up to $900 Million for Small and Medium Business Support
item.description: Kyrgyzstan aims to attract $800-900 million by 2030 to support its small and medium-sized enterprises (SME) program. Funds will focus on improving access to finance, reducing administrative burdens, and developing regional production and digital services. The program addresses issues like high credit costs and legal protection.

item.title: Trump Desires Russia-Ukraine Peace Deal Before January, Reports Indicate
item.description: Former US President Donald Trump reportedly wants Russia and Ukraine to reach a peace agreement before January. This desire is linked to the Democrats potentially gaining control of both houses of Congress. However, Putin has refused negotiations following attacks on the Crimean bridge.

item.title: Tajikistan and US Sign $78 Million Health Cooperation Agreement
item.description: Tajikistan and the United States have signed a five-year health cooperation program in Dushanbe, with a total funding of $78 million. The US will provide $38 million, and Tajikistan will contribute $40 million. Funds will target HIV, tuberculosis, infectious diseases, laboratory diagnostics, and epidemiological surveillance through the end of FY2030.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Sees Several Personnel Changes, Including New Deputy Minister and US Ambassador
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has experienced several personnel shifts over the past week. Chyngyz Esengul uulu has been appointed as the First Deputy Minister of Culture, Information, and Youth Policy. Other appointments include new akims and the US Ambassador to the Kyrgyz Republic.

item.title: Russian President Putin Visits Tajikistan for Talks on Migration and Security
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin visited Tajikistan for talks with President Emomali Rahmon. Discussions covered labor migration, regional security, economic cooperation, and the Russian military base in Tajikistan. They also addressed educational and cultural initiatives, including a center for gifted children and a drama theater.

item.title: Afghan Ambassador: 85-90% of Refugees Have Returned from Pakistan
item.description: Afghanistan's Ambassador to Pakistan, Sardar Ahmad Shakeeb, stated that approximately 85 to 90 percent of Afghan refugees have returned home. He conveyed this during a meeting with the new UNHCR head in Pakistan, Noriko Tagaki, emphasizing the Islamic Emirate's efforts to facilitate their return and reception.

item.title: Afghan UN Missions Demand Rights of Afghan People Central to International Engagement
item.description: Permanent Afghan missions to the UN in Geneva, New York, and Vienna stated that international engagement must support a political process led by the Afghan people to achieve legitimate governance. They emphasized that the rights and demands of Afghans, including women and girls, should be central to all interactions, warning against normalizing the exclusion of women from public life.

item.title: Bishkek Construction Halted Over Pre-Completion Apartment Sales
item.description: A 16-story residential complex construction in Bishkek has been halted, and the developer fined 200,000 soms. The Ministry of Construction suspended the company's license for selling apartments before the foundational zero cycle was completed, a violation of regulations designed to protect buyer funds.
